Lazyeyez:

This mass quoting is prior to the finalized thought on those exact claims, youre trying to back your argument and dismissing the articles conclusion

Reuters is a news agency, meaning that if you are looking for a “conclusion” to an article … that’s always at the bottom of the entire article. Not in the middle and certainly not in the middle of a sentence taken out of context.

If you want a “conclusion” to an article that was written entirely to be a “Here’s the factual reporting of what has happened” (which means that there is no conclusion), the conclusion would be as follows:

  • AI is being pushed prematurely onto the market for medical devices.
  • Medical devices that previously had no AI require no additional FDA approval for any AI additions added to said devices.
  • FDA is underfunded and cannot thoroughly test whether AI is as safe as it is marketed as being.
  • 1,401 of the reports filed between 2021 and 2025 mentioned AI as part of the complaint.
  • When comparing certain medical devices with the only difference being one had AI and one didn’t, the recall rate for the AI-product had twice the recall rate to its non-AI counterpart.
  • TruDI and other companies’ AI products regularly misidentify body parts.

Not entirely sure what this has to do with WoW though, but it is a good demonstration that AI isn’t what it is marketed as.

Supersonic:

Did they create the world soul saga with AI?

No. They have been pretty open about the fact that the World Saga was Metzen’s idea and he worked with what they already had and adapted it to work as a longer storyline (Blizzard’s development pattern have usually been three expansions: maintaining, updating, and work on the current live; build and develop the next expansion; and make plans for the one after that; the World Saga is only really ‘unique’ in that they wanted to make the storyline build for two expansions with a conclusion in the third instead of build-conclusion-build-conclusion that they have done in the past).

Microsoft is shifting from buying frontier intelligence to building it. They unveiled seven in-house models, led by MAI-Thinking-1, at Build on June 2.

To date, they have been “renting” AI from Anthropic and Open AI. Owning its models lets Microsoft stop paying a toll on work it could do in-house.

At Microsoft’s scale, trimming the cost of every query will be the difference between thin margins and fat ones. But owning artificial intelligence means paying for it up front, and Microsoft is already carrying heavy bills for data centers and chips. They need to cover these costs somehow and I suspect layoffs may be to bridge that gap.

Long term? I am just speculating, but believe as Microsoft’s cost per token drops (once their AI is in-house, they will deploy AI more in all its companies, including the games division.
